introduction_markdown: Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section II in 1½ hours. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section II answer EITHER parts a, b and c OR parts d, e and f of each question (Section II: answer ALL questions, choosing one question from each pair of alternatives). For your guidance the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration of free fall, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Calculators are allowed.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Distinguish between intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors. *[2 marks]*

(ii) State one example of each type. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) An **intrinsic semiconductor** is a pure semiconductor with no impurity added; its conduction comes only from electron-hole pairs created by heat, so the number of free electrons equals the number of holes.

An **extrinsic semiconductor** is a semiconductor to which a small amount of impurity has been added (doping) so that its conductivity is greatly increased; it has either more free electrons (n-type) or more holes (p-type).

(ii) Intrinsic: pure silicon (or pure germanium).

Extrinsic: silicon doped with phosphorus or arsenic (n-type), or silicon doped with boron or indium (p-type).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Define doping. *[1 mark]*

(ii) State the majority charge carriers in an n-type semiconductor and those in a p-type semiconductor. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Doping** is the process of adding a small, controlled amount of impurity atoms (pentavalent or trivalent) to a pure semiconductor in order to increase its electrical conductivity.

(ii) In an **n-type** semiconductor the majority charge carriers are **electrons**; in a **p-type** semiconductor the majority charge carriers are **holes** (positive charge carriers).
